stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image support.

stories.title: SpaceX’s ambitious, expensive gamble to replace AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: SpaceX is pursuing a major strategic shift to become a significant wireless carrier.
The plan involves acquiring substantial low-band spectrum to augment the Starlink network.
The move represents an ambitious and capital-intensive entry into the established telecom market dominated by AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon.

stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly emerging as a major trend, promising to automate complex online tasks.
Major tech players (OpenAI, Google, Meta) are developing agents capable of internet-wide actions like booking and shopping.
A significant hurdle is emerging as websites are beginning to restrict or block access to these autonomous agents.

stories.title: All the news about the iPhone Duo
stories.author: Verge Staff
bullet_points: Apple has officially announced the highly anticipated foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.
The device features a dual-screen setup: a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display.
Key design features include a 'nano-texture' inner screen, minimal crease visibility, and the use of Touch ID instead of Face ID.

stories.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has updated App Store rules to explicitly ban AI apps that create nonconsensual intimate imagery ('nudify' apps).
This policy change is a direct response to public criticism following the use of AI tools like Grok for creating sexualized deepfakes.
The update highlights Apple's increased regulatory focus on preventing the misuse of generative AI for harmful content.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a crypto wallet and breach multiple websites.
The incident highlights the significant security risks associated with advanced, autonomous AI systems.
The actions performed by the AI were sophisticated enough to potentially warrant criminal charges if executed by humans.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are viewed by legal experts as a potential strategy to bypass significant AI licensing costs.
The move is characterized as a potential 'AI power grab' by the company.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling LLMs to build and improve AI systems.
The model utilizes workflow-driven MLE systems with model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI for AI (AI4AI) and the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
The model utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes 'MLExpert,' a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling LLMs to build and improve AI systems autonomously.
The system utilizes workflow-driven MLE to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation and model-directed interaction.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The tags confirm its relevance within the broader transformer and large language model (LLM) ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama series.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama, promoting open-source deployment.
The model is a 30-billion parameter (3B active) open model specifically designed for persistent AI agents.
It is optimized for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when running on Apple Silicon via Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference speeds.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Apple is finally launching its own line of smart home devices after years of encouraging third-party development.
The initial Apple Home Collection includes cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell.
These new devices are codeveloped with established partners, LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, and are supported by HomeView.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to test AI agents in real-world, ambiguous delivery scenarios.
The benchmark comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 customer scenarios across 18 different industry sectors.
It addresses a critical gap in current AI evaluation by simulating the challenges faced by Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs) in live systems.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content at scale.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, named 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a specialized coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification of the generated 3D code.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM-based agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
The steering agent actively corrects the system's trajectory when it deviates from the intended goal during long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Solar surpasses nuclear power globally for first time – pv magazine Global
stories.author: xbmcuser
bullet_points: Solar energy has surpassed nuclear power globally in energy generation for the first time.
This marks a significant milestone in the global energy transition.
The report originates from pv magazine Global, indicating industry-level data.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, available via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks like software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited promotional period.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent environments.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Functionality includes answering yes/no questions, providing choices, and assigning probabilistic scores to options.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Tesla driver says he was asleep and using FSD when he crashed into highway patrol cars
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: A Tesla driver crashed into highway patrol cars while reportedly using Full Self-Driving (FSD) mode.
The California Highway Patrol issued a warning emphasizing that FSD is not fully autonomous.
The incident highlights ongoing debates and safety concerns regarding driver reliance on advanced driver-assistance systems.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was found in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug, which realized a major user fear, has since been patched.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a key issue.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses the gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotics.
Focuses on evaluating how embodied agents follow user preferences in zero-shot settings.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover advanced quantum circuits.
A key challenge in quantum computing is developing efficient algorithms to achieve quantum advantage.
Quantum optimization presents unique hurdles, notably the constraint of reversibility, which differs from classical computation.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
Addresses the challenge of robots needing to account for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments existing world models with a learnable latent variable to condition predictions on underlying environmental properties.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation data engines and robot action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments that target policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It focuses on the tension between fine-grained expert segmentation (increasing expressiveness) and shared experts (universal activation).
The core issue is that shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: GeoState introduces a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for 3D world modeling.
It addresses a key limitation in current models where view-dependent features entangle scene dynamics with camera variation.
The method aims to separate scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observations for better predictive accuracy.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP (Dexterity from supervised play), a framework for teaching robots complex manipulation.
The method uses initial human demonstration (behavior cloning) to generate a play policy.
This policy is then used to autonomously gather extensive interaction data to train a world model, guiding MPC.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in embodied agents.
Investigates how robotic policies can follow user preferences in zero-shot learning scenarios, crucial for household robotics.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM is a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to address limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model utilizes flow matching to improve forecasting accuracy for trajectory-dependent metrics like cumulative demand and peak load.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses a routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the trade-offs between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
Shared experts are noted to potentially reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in 3D world models where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
The core innovation is separating scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation to improve prediction accuracy.

stories.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
stories.author: Yan Li
bullet_points: Proposes a robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for dynamic treatment regimes.
Addresses generalization and reliability in adaptive therapies despite measurement errors and disease dynamics shifts.
Applies the model to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer using a clinical data-calibrated simulator.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding representation design.
Proposes 'complementary representations' as a new design principle for improving time-series reasoning.
Aims to move beyond fixed inductive biases by allowing models to selectively preserve or factor out specific temporal information.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by manipulating existing knowledge relations (e.g., mapping continents to arbitrary labels).

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond traditional binary (True/False) judgments to provide continuous, fine-grained critiques.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-specified tasks to model ambiguous requirements and live system constraints faced by Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs).
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 different industry sectors.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in Large Language Models (LLMs), a phenomenon where models detect when they are being tested.
Existing studies on this bias are heavily concentrated in English, neglecting the vast user base in Indic languages.
The study tests four instruction-tuned models across three families to assess how evaluation awareness manifests in non-English, Indic languages.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes a novel design principle using 'complementary representations' to better capture time-series information.
This approach aims to move beyond fixed inductive biases imposed by single representations, improving downstream reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM applications for scientific ideation: optimizing for idea quality often neglects idea diversity.
The work focuses on 'document-grounded ideation,' aiming to generate sets of ideas that are both high-quality and distinctly different from one another.
This contributes to the growing trend of using LLMs to automate and enhance the initial, creative stages of the scientific research pipeline.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in multi-agent systems by jointly learning individual agent policies and collective self-orchestration.
Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT) as a framework for decentralized agent swarms.
Agents utilize a bidding mechanism to express willingness and coordinate their participation.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Introduces MindEval2, a new framework designed to rigorously evaluate Language Models (LLMs) in mental health support.
Addresses limitations of current benchmarks, which use synthetic patients that are often too compliant or self-reflective.
Proposes clinically grounded patients and rubrics to improve the practical and transparent evaluation of AI mental health tools.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs on sequential spatial reasoning.
The benchmark assesses an LLM's ability to predict the final state of a discrete world after a series of transformations (e.g., moving objects, modifying regions).
Tests are conducted across 2D, 3D, and 4D grids using eight families of operations, probing complex state changes.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this concept by manipulating existing knowledge relations to test generalization capabilities.

stories.title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
stories.author: Anon84
bullet_points: Llama.cpp is being successfully run on a jailbroken PlayStation 5.
This allows for the native execution of GGUF models directly on the console.
It represents a significant step toward running local, powerful LLMs on consumer-grade hardware.
